Aspartame is an artificial sweetener used in many diet foods and beverages. Over the years, there has been significant research into its safety. Major health organizations, including the FDA, EFSA, and WHO, have reviewed the evidence and concluded that aspartame is safe for the general population when consumed within established daily intake limits. 

There have been claims that aspartame is a neurotoxin, causes cancer, or is linked to brain tumors, but these claims are not supported by the majority of scientific evidence. Some individuals with the genetic disorder phenylketonuria (PKU) must avoid aspartame because they cannot metabolize phenylalanine, one of its breakdown products. However, for most people, aspartame has not been proven to cause health issues.
